title: Touchpad fault
shortDescription: The control panel detected a stuck or shorted key.
fullDescription:
Jenn-Air microwaves show F1 when a button reads pressed for more than 60 seconds. Cleaning around the keypad and resetting power often clears it.

If the code returns, the touchpad ribbon or membrane needs replacement.

fixSteps.title: Replace touchpad
fixSteps.instruction: If error returns, replace membrane keypad assembly.

whenToCallPro: If unsure about discharging the high-voltage capacitor.

faq.a: Yes, F1 is a control fault only.

title: Oven temperature sensor open
fullDescription:
F2 on a Jenn-Air convection microwave indicates the oven temperature sensor is reading open. This disables convection mode but the unit may still microwave.

Replace the temperature probe.
whenToCallPro: Built-in models often require pulling the entire unit.

faq.q: Can I still use microwave mode?
faq.a: Usually yes, but get it fixed soon.

title: Oven temperature sensor shorted
fullDescription: F3 indicates the cavity temperature sensor is shorted. Convection cooking is disabled. Replace the sensor and the corresponding harness if pinched.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the cavity probe and check harness routing.

whenToCallPro: Built-in models recommended for pro service.

title: Humidity sensor failure
fullDescription: F5 is shown when the humidity sensor used for sensor-cook modes returns invalid readings. Cleaning grease residue from the sensor often resolves it.

fixSteps.title: Clean cavity vents
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe vent slots and around sensor location.

whenToCallPro: If cleaning fails to clear the code.

faq.q: Can I still use timed cooking?
faq.a: Yes, only sensor mode is affected.

title: Line voltage fault
shortDescription: Voltage outside normal range during operation.
fullDescription: F6 means the microwave detected line voltage that drifted outside spec while operating. Often coincides with brownouts or overloaded circuits.
whenToCallPro: Electrician if voltage is out of spec.

faq.a: A line conditioner may, but a basic strip will not.

title: Door switch fault
shortDescription: Door interlocks not seeing consistent open/closed state.
fullDescription:
F7 is reported when the three door interlock switches do not agree. Misaligned door, debris in latch, or a failed switch are common causes.

This must be repaired before microwaving - the interlocks are a safety system.

fixSteps.title: Inspect door
fixSteps.instruction: Check that the door closes squarely against the cavity.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the offending interlock after capacitor discharge.

faq.a: Never - it is a safety lockout.

title: Cooling fan fault
fullDescription: F8 alerts that the microwave detected the magnetron cooling fan is not spinning. This must be fixed quickly to avoid magnetron damage.

fixSteps.title: Clean filters
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and degrease the charcoal/grease filters.

faq.a: Try first - sometimes that restores airflow.

title: Magnetron over-temperature
shortDescription: Thermal protector tripped on the magnetron.
fullDescription: F9 occurs when the magnetron thermal cutoff trips. After cool-down the unit may resume, but a recurring F9 means failing magnetron, blocked airflow, or weak fan.
whenToCallPro: If F9 returns within a few cycles.

title: Communication error
shortDescription: UI and main control not communicating.
fullDescription: F0 indicates the touchpad and the main relay/control board lost serial communication. Reseating the ribbon cable and a power cycle resolves most cases.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon
fixSteps.instruction: Open control housing and reseat ribbon connector.

title: Convection element fault
fullDescription: FC reports when the convection element circuit is open or shorted. Replacement of the element or its relay resolves the fault.

fixSteps.title: Replace element
fixSteps.instruction: Service replacement of the convection element.
